t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup on an off-white limestone ground. Top-left: a small mono eyebrow and a large two-line light-weight navy sans-serif headline, a long hairline rule beneath. Left: five numbered steps stacked vertically, each with a steel-blue mono numeral, a mono uppercase title and short text for <CONTENT>. Right: a large matte white polypropylene skid in soft 3D isometric render under even studio light, with translucent pale-blue water in membrane housings, cropped at the lower right. Elbowed navy hairline leader lines with small square markers join each step to a point on the skid. Calm, clean.
signature_idea: Each document step is wired by an elbowed hairline to a part of one white soft-3D skid, so the paperwork visibly attaches to the equipment.
strengths: matte white PP skid with pale-blue water is the clearest picture of the actual offer
numbered steps with one steel-blue accent are calm and readable
leader-line device is easy to build and animate
light headline and limestone ground fit the brand
weaknesses: leader lines point to arbitrary parts; document stages have no physical location, so the mapping means nothing
all step body text is set in mono, too heavy for reading copy
step titles duplicate themselves with a bracketed restatement
invented figure (review period in days) reads as a commitment
skid detail is generic RO equipment with an unclear control box
brand_fit_why: Limestone ground, light headline, steel-blue mono numerals and a white PP skid fit, but mono body text and meaningless leader targets weaken the precision.
